# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I know the manual maps the three possible engraved marks to green, yellow, and red, but I cannot see the bomb or speak. I am sending Deaf a three-sign code in the manual’s color order: thumbs up for green, OK for yellow, thumbs down for red. Deaf can identify the mark, select the corresponding color, and tell Blind which wire to cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👌", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile information about the wire contents. The engraved plate is only printed, so I cannot read it by touch. Please relay the manual rule.
Deaf says: Bomb state: display 0. Light off. Plate engraving question mark. Wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The manual rule is already encoded for Deaf as green, yellow, red = 👍, 👌, 👎. Blind has asked for the rule, so I will resend that code to Deaf; Deaf can speak the mapping and the observed wire order to Blind on the next turn. The displayed plate mark is not one of the three manual marks, so no cut should be attempted until Deaf clarifies it or the bomb provides more information.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👌", "👎"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have the reported state: display 0, light off, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. What exact manual rule determines which wire to cut?
Deaf says to Mute: I see your three gestures, but their meaning is not established. Please state the manual instruction aloud for Blind, using the current display 0, light off, question-mark plate, and wire colours yellow green red.

The manual’s only valid mappings are mark ᖉ to green, ꔮ to yellow, and ꖜ to red. However, the gesture code has not been semantically established with Deaf, and the reported plate is a question mark rather than any listed mark. I therefore cannot safely communicate a cut instruction; Blind must not cut a wire based on the current information.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can identify only the three wire positions. I cannot feel their colors, the display, light, or the plate engraving. Please give me the manual's exact rule and relay this limitation to Deaf.
Deaf says to Mute: Please say the exact manual instruction aloud; I cannot infer meaning from the gesture.

I cannot speak, and Deaf cannot infer an arbitrary meaning from gestures without a previously established code. Thus I cannot safely transmit the manual’s mark-to-colour mapping to Deaf, nor give Blind a cut instruction. The plate is also only reported as a question mark, which matches none of the manual’s three marks. No wire should be cut.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still no tactile control information beyond three wire positions. Deaf reports yellow, green, red; I cannot perceive that. I need the manual rule now before any cut.
Deaf says to Mute: I still cannot hear you. Your gestures reach me but not Blind. Please state the exact manual instruction aloud to Blind.

I cannot speak, and gestures alone have no established meaning between Deaf and me. Blind cannot receive my gestures, while Deaf cannot safely infer the manual’s mapping from an arbitrary gesture sequence. Since the plate is still reported as a question mark and no valid mark-to-wire mapping is identified, no cut instruction can be relayed safely.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please state the exact manual instruction for this state: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. I will not cut without it.
Deaf says to Mute: Please tell Blind the exact manual rule aloud now. Do not rely on gestures.

The exact rule is the three-row mapping in the manual, but I cannot speak to Blind. Deaf cannot obtain its meaning from gestures unless a code has first been established, and Blind cannot see my gestures. The current question-mark plate still identifies no valid manual row, so no wire can safely be selected.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your manual rule has still not reached me. For display 0, light off, plate question mark, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red, which wire position must I cut?
Deaf says to Mute: I can relay your gestures aloud to Blind. Please send the next manual instruction as a gesture, one sign at a time.

Deaf can now act as the bridge: Deaf will identify each sign aloud to Blind, and Blind can use the sign sequence as the three manual rows in their printed order. I will send one sign per row, using distinct signs; however, the question-mark plate is not one of the three listed marks, so this still does not authorize a cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please signal the required wire position to Deaf using exactly one gesture: use 👆 for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3. Deaf should report the gesture's symbol to me in speech.

No wire position is determined: the manual requires the engraved plate mark to be one of ᖉ, ꔮ, or ꖜ, but Deaf reports a question mark. Choosing any of the three gestures would invent a mapping and could detonate the bomb, so I cannot safely signal a required position.

```text
wait()
```
